title: Security Ops: Pen Test + Vulnerability Remediation Plan - Zenith Health
summary: Review of recent third-party pen test for Redwood-hosted deployment, discussion of remediation timelines, vuln triage process, evidence for SOC 2 / ISO controls, RBAC/SSO flows, audit logging retention, KMS envelope encryption, and recommended patching cadence for application and infra components.
next_steps: Redwood to send annotated pen-test report with prioritized CVEs (Maya) - by 2025-04-29
Zenith to provide list of in-scope endpoints and expected P1/P2 SLAs - Ben - by 2025-04-25
Schedule follow-up technical deep dive on KMS integration and key rotation with SEs - Carlos & Tom - week of 2025-05-05
action_items: Maya: Share redacted pen test report PDF + mitigation mapping - due 2025-04-29
Carlos: Prepare KV cache and prefix caching security notes and sample config - due 2025-05-02
Ben: Send Zenith's vuln mgmt runbook and patch window constraints - due 2025-04-25
Priya: Confirm compliance evidence needed for SOC2 auditor (logs, rotation docs) - due 2025-04-28
Tom: Provide list of allowed IP blocks for VPC peering to evaluate lock-down options - due 2025-04-27
questions: Do you support customer-managed key rotation via KMS/HSM?
How granular is RBAC for model access and who can see raw transcripts?
What patch cadence does Redwood recommend for critical OS vulnerabilities on Dedicated?
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-22 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Recording: fireflies_link_placeholder
Attendees: Maya T., Carlos N., Leah P. (Redwood) — Aisha R., Ben L., Priya D., Tom K., Sam O. (Zenith)

Summary / quick notes (auto): Maya opened, agenda set: pen test findings, remediation, SDLC, patching cadence, audit evidence.

[00:00:12] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we know schedules are tight so we'll go through the pen test highlights first then remediation plan. Carlos is with me for the technical deep dive.
[00:00:27] Aisha: Thanks, Maya. We got the high level earlier but want to make sure there's a clear timeline and proof points for SOC2 audit. Also want to flag data residency constraints for some PHI-adjacent workloads.
[00:00:42] Carlos: Yep, understood. We reviewed the pen test; note that some of the items were low severity config issues and a handful of CVSS 7+ items that are infra related. We'll call out what's in hosted vs Dedicated.
[00:01:05] Ben: Quick note, Zenith's expectation: P1s need to be remediated or mitigated within 14 days, P2 within 45. Is that compatible with your release cadence?
[00:01:20] Maya: We're generally able to meet that SLAs for Dedicated customers; for hosted customers we have a managed patching pipeline — for critical infra vulns we do emergency rollouts, but we'll need to align on change windows.
[00:01:36] Tom: Can you explain what 'emergency rollouts' look like? Does that require downtime? We have production inference calls at all hours.
[00:01:48] Carlos: Most of the time we do live rolling updates with zero downtime — the serving runtime supports having a mix of versions during rollout. Occasionally a kernel or driver patch on the underlying host may require brief failed-over restarts, but we aim for graceful degradation.
[00:02:10] Priya: For the audit, we need evidence of patching cadence and the rollback plan. Also a log of who approved the emergency change.
[00:02:25] Leah: We'll provide the change control exports and an anonymized approval trail, and map that to your SOC2 control ids.
[00:02:39] Aisha: On the pen test specifics — one of the findings flagged an exposed admin endpoint with weak auth on a staging host. Was that a misconfiguration or something in the app?
[00:02:55] Carlos: That was a misconfiguration — the staging environment had a default route and the auth middleware wasn't enforced due to an env var flip during a deploy. We've already patched the staging guard and added an automated check in CI to fail builds if the NODE_ENV-like setting isn't set.
[00:03:16] Ben: Nice, can you show the CI check? We need to see it runs as part of the secure SDLC.
[00:03:28] Carlos: I'll share the snippet after the call; it's a pre-deploy linter that asserts env and RBAC rules. It's in the onboarding repo — we'll redact secrets.
[00:03:42] [00:03:50] Sam: A question about KMS — we heard you support customer-managed keys, but is there support for HSM-backed rotation and bring-your-own-key?
[00:03:58] Maya: Short answer: yes for Dedicated and Private deployments we support KMS integrations and can do BYOK/HSM flows; for hosted we offer either Redwood-managed keys or a dedicated customer KMS integration for enterprise plans. There's a small ops process to set up the key trust relationship.
[00:04:22] Tom: How often do you rotate? Our baseline requirement is 90-day rotation for data keys and yearly for master keys.
[00:04:33] Carlos: We support configurable rotation; typical config is 90 days for envelope keys and 365 for the master. We can provide rotation logs as part of audit export.
[00:04:45] Priya: For SOC2 we'll need the log format and retention window — how long do you keep key usage logs?
[00:04:54] Leah: By default our hosted plan retains audit logs for 180 days; enterprise retention is configurable — we can push to your log store or S3 with lifecycle rules for longer retention.
[00:05:06] Aisha: Okay. Next pen test item: S3 bucket permissions. The report flagged overly permissive ACLs for a model-artifacts bucket used during training. Is that still open?
[00:05:20] Carlos: That was in a historical pipeline — we've updated bucket policies to block public ACLs and added a pre-commit check on deployment to verify policy. The artifact pipeline now uses presigned URLs with short TTL.
[00:05:38] Ben: Good. Could you include the policy change diff in the deliverables? Auditor wants specifics.
[00:05:45] Maya: Yes, we'll include the policy diff and a one-pager mapping changes to the finding IDs.
[00:05:56] [00:06:05] Aisha: There's an item about insufficient RBAC for transcript access — who at Redwood can see raw user transcripts and how is that restricted?
[00:06:18] Carlos: Access to raw transcripts is limited by RBAC; only roles with "support_read" and "security_audit" can view content. For Hosted we log access and require SSO+MFA. For Dedicated/Private you can restrict via VPC and your SCIM groups. We also redact PII where requested.
[00:06:40] Tom: Can we have a list of the role names and a sample access audit?
[00:06:47] Leah: We'll export a sample audit CSV showing role, actor, time, and resource, scrubbed for PHI.
[00:06:55] [00:07:10] Ben: Pen test also flagged outdated OSS deps in one microservice — looks like a 3rd party lib with known CVE. What's your remediation flow? Do you force dependency updates?
[00:07:23] Carlos: Our pipeline runs weekly dependency scans using Snyk and a few custom signatures; we create tickets automatically and triage by severity. For vulnerable libs with active exploitability, we push a hotfix branch and do an emergency release. We do not force updates automatically because we need testing for behavioral changes, but we block merges if a vulnerability exceeds severity threshold until approved by security owner.
[00:07:52] Priya: What's your SLA on turning a scan result into a ticket and then into a fix? That matters for our security acceptance criteria.
[00:08:03] Maya: We create tickets within 24 hours of discovery. Prioritization is P1/P2 as discussed; remediation depends on complexity but critical ones are fast-tracked. We'll include a chart of mean time to remediation for the last 12 months.
[00:08:18] Aisha: We also want to know your dependency pinning policy and signed artifacts to avoid supply chain issues.
[00:08:26] Carlos: We pin dependencies in our build manifests, use reproducible builds where possible, and sign release artifacts. For third-party models, we record provenance and checksums.
[00:08:38] [00:08:50] Sam: Let's talk patch cadence on infra hosts and GPU drivers — the pen test report had a driver-level CVE rated high. Do you manage those for Dedicated?
[00:09:01] Carlos: For Dedicated, infra patches are part of the managed service; we run monthly maintenance windows and emergency driver updates when needed. We notify customers and can schedule out-of-hours windows. For Private we provide the playbooks and ops runbooks for customers to run.
[00:09:23] Tom: If we want more aggressive patching, can we opt-in to a weekly kernel update?
[00:09:29] Maya: Yes, that's an add-on for Dedicated — we can do accelerated patching with tighter change controls. We'll add pricing to the follow-up.
[00:09:38] [00:09:50] Priya: Another pen test note — missing SIEM integration for some events. We saw authentication failures not being exported.
[00:09:58] Leah: We have native integrations with major SIEM providers; export covers auth events, key usage, admin API calls, and model invocation logs. We can also stream to your Kafka or S3 bucket.
[00:10:15] Ben: What about log retention and tamper-evidence? Need to show the auditor it's immutable for the required window.
[00:10:24] Carlos: We support append-only logs with write-once buckets or integrated WORM storage for enterprise; also provide signed log digests for tamper-evidence.
[00:10:36] [00:10:45] Aisha: On data residency: some workloads must remain in EU DCs. Can you guarantee model serving and logs stay in-region?
[00:10:55] Maya: Yes, we can pin region routing and store logs in-region for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we have region controls for enterprise customers; we'll confirm the AWS region mapping and provide a region binding SLA in the doc.
[00:11:12] Sam: One operational question: during a remediation we need to prove to our auditor that the fix didn't change output semantics for model responses. Do you run evals tied to the release?
[00:11:24] Carlos: We have a regression harness — Redwood Optimize can run diffs on prompt/response pairs and flag quality regressions tied to model or runtime changes. We'll run that as part of the canary and provide the eval results.
[00:11:39] [00:11:50] Ben: Going back to the pen test priorities — can you confirm which items were "exploit only in local lab" vs "reachable from internet"? Auditor wants that level of granularity.
[00:11:59] Carlos: We'll annotate each finding with exploitability context and proof-of-concept level — we have that in the full report. We'll mark those that are publicly reachable vs internal.
[00:12:14] Maya: High-level remediation plan: 1) Immediate mitigations for P1s (config/ACL changes) within two business days, 2) Hotfix releases for code-level P1s within 14 days, 3) CI/CD policy improvements in 30 days, 4) longer-term platform hardening and automations in the next quarter.
[00:12:35] Priya: Sounds reasonable; we want owners for each.
[00:12:40] Maya: We'll assign internal owners and share the mitigation tracker.
[00:12:45] [00:13:00] Aisha: A question about proof for SOC2 control about vendor management — does Redwood maintain a vendor risk register and do you do periodic pen tests yourself?
[00:13:11] Leah: Redwood runs annual third-party penetration tests and quarterly internal vulnerability scans; we can share summary reports and attestations, subject to NDAs. We also maintain a vendor register and scope docs.
[00:13:25] Tom: For the patch windows, what's the communication path? We need an RFC and a calendar invite with outage SLA.
[00:13:33] Maya: We have a designated Customer Ops channel, RFC repo, and we send 72/24/6 hour notifications depending on severity. For emergency patches we do real-time Slack and a postmortem.
[00:13:50] [00:14:05] Ben: About RBAC granularity — can you do attribute-based access so we can limit transcripts to person-role and project?
[00:14:15] Carlos: We support attribute-based policies for Dedicated/Private; for Hosted we have role + groups via SCIM mapping. We'll share sample policy templates.
[00:14:29] Priya: Also need to confirm who has access to raw model weights and that they are encrypted at rest.
[00:14:38] Carlos: Model artifacts are stored encrypted with envelope encryption; access is controlled and audited. We can provide a list of teams with access and the KMS logs.
[00:14:50] [00:15:10] Aisha: Can you walk through a specific P1 example from the pen test so we can validate the remediation chain?
[00:15:22] Carlos: Sure. Finding 01: Auth bypass on staging admin endpoint. Root cause: missing middleware boolean due to a deploy flag, exploit: local low-auth access. Fix: added middleware enforcement, CI check, and network ACL to block staging from public net. Proof: we've included curl-based PoC and the fixed response code in the report.
[00:15:50] Ben: Ok show the timeline for that one?
[00:15:55] Leah: That was detected on 2025-04-10, patch deployed 2025-04-13, validation on 2025-04-14. We'll include timestamps.
[00:16:06] [00:16:20] Sam: Anything outstanding that we should worry about?
[00:16:25] Carlos: There are two code-level P2s in a microservice that require a small refactor; low blast radius but non-trivial testing. We'll aim to get them into the next sprint.
[00:16:37] Priya: For the auditor we need proof of design decisions — architecture diagrams and control mappings.
[00:16:44] Maya: We'll include architecture diagrams with in-scope boundaries and a control matrix mapping pen test findings to SOC2 control IDs.
[00:16:58] [00:17:15] Ben: A question re: secrets management — do you use a central secrets manager for runtime credentials?
[00:17:23] Carlos: Yes, we use vault-like secret storage for runtime keys and ephemeral tokens for the serving runtime; secrets are never checked into git and are provisioned via secure agents.
[00:17:34] Aisha: How does that interact with customer-managed KMS?
[00:17:40] Carlos: We wrap secrets with envelope encryption using your KMS keys if you choose BYOK; access still controlled by our agent identity.
[00:17:51] [00:18:05] Tom: Any chance of sharing the backlog of security work we can review? A list of upcoming hardening items would help us accept the roadmap.
[00:18:14] Leah: We'll send a redacted security roadmap and the mitigation tracker.
[00:18:22] [00:18:40] Maya: Quick pivot — patch cadence recommendations: for infra hosts we recommend monthly baseline plus emergency hotfixes; for drivers/GPU firmware we recommend quarterly checks and emergency updates if CVE exploited in wild. For app dependencies we recommend weekly scans and P1 patching within 14 days.
[00:19:02] Ben: Can you provide historical MTTR numbers for the last 6 months?
[00:19:08] Maya: Yes, we'll include MTTD/MTTR metrics and ticket examples.
[00:19:20] [00:19:45] Aisha: About evidence for auditors — can you provide a sample set: 1) pen-test attestation, 2) patch calendar, 3) CI check logs, 4) audit log export, 5) KMS rotation logs.
[00:19:59] Leah: Affirmative — we'll produce a package with those items, redacted as appropriate.
[00:20:10] Carlos: Also note we can sign an evidence bundle under NDA for your auditor.
[00:20:20] [00:20:35] Sam: For the SIEM, can you push detection rules for auth anomalies? We want default alerts when there are anomalies in transcript reads.
[00:20:44] Carlos: We have a rule set we can export and customize — for example, alert on unusual admin API activity or multiple failed SSO attempts from unusual geos.
[00:20:58] Ben: Ok that covers most of the findings. Next steps?
[00:21:05] Maya: We'll send the annotated pen test with mitigation mapping and a delivery timeline. Carlos will run the KMS deep dive with Tom. Leah will prepare the SOC2 evidence bundle.
[00:21:18] Priya: Can we get a follow-up call focused on compliance artifacts with our auditor included?
[00:21:25] Maya: Yes, set a date and we'll invite our compliance lead.
[00:21:32] [00:21:45] Aisha: Anything we should have done differently as a customer to avoid the staging misconfig?
[00:21:54] Carlos: Two things — network isolation for non-prod and enforceable CI flags as gate checks. We can help automate both.
[00:22:08] Ben: One last item: supply chain — can you provide SBOMs for the microservices in scope?
[00:22:17] Leah: We can provide SBOMs and provenance for the model artifacts; some items may require NDAs.
[00:22:27] [00:22:40] Aisha: Thanks all. Appreciate the partner approach. We'll review the deliverables and confirm timelines.
[00:22:50] Maya: Thanks everyone, action items recap: Maya send pen-test PDF + policy diffs; Carlos share CI checks and KMS deep-dive plan; Leah send SOC2 evidence package; Ben/Tom send in-scope endpoints and patch window constraints.
[00:23:12] Meeting ends but participants stay on for async Q&A (approx 39 more minutes of side-chat and clarifications, captured in raw notes):
[00:23:30] [00:24:02] Ben: Quick — is there a way to suppress debug logs that sometimes leak user identifiers?
[00:24:10] Carlos: We have log scrubbing in the ingestion pipeline; debug logs are routed to ephemeral dev buckets and redacted by pattern rules.
[00:24:30] [00:25:00] Priya: If we need a longer log retention window for the audit, can you export to our S3 with 7-year lifecycle?
[00:25:08] Leah: Yes we can set up log archival and lifecycle policies to match your retention need.
[00:26:15] Tom: Follow up on NAT traversal for VPC peering — we'll send the network topologies.
[00:26:22] Maya: Great, we'll review and confirm peering options.
[00:27:40] [00:28:00] Carlos: One tip — enabling prefix/KV cache invalidation hooks helped a customer mitigate stale auth tokens after rotation. We'll share an example hook.
[00:28:20] Ben: Sounds good. Thanks team.
